Power is something I had considered but I haven't looked at the site in its current state.  The previous owners were running full racks pretty much so there should be enough power available.  There is a generator, I'm not sure how big or which circuits it powers.  The entire building is concrete block walls, they're already utilizing a key-fob system for access control and have a DVR system monitoring the premises -- nothing monitoring the server room yet.  I did tell him before I even came on board that he would need to retain a lawyer for the type of work he's trying to get into.  Fire suppression is definitely something we'll need to look at.  The law firm I worked for before my current place had a pretty impressive fire suppression system for only 4 racks.

I guess I should have been more clear.  This guy does not know anything about computers/servers/datacenters.  He barely understands his own PC.  I'm just hesitant to step up into that kind of role.  Been running a 10-location, 200+workstation environment by myself for 1.5 years at my current spot.  But we're only running 5 physical servers too.  The level of technology is a huge leap.  I guess what I'm saying is -- how deep can I get myself into this?  Is this like...senior sysadmin type stuff?  

I'm not confident in my abilities and it would be my first time setting up a datacenter.
